# readonly-return-mutation (MUT202)

Family: Mutation & State (MUT) · Heuristic · Off by default · Severity `error` (a bug) · No automatic fix

Mutating a shared object returned by a declared `readonly-returns` producer or `@lru_cache`, directly or through the functions that return it.

!!! note "Heuristic"

    This rule is heuristic: a premise of its claim can be open ("What a report states" lists them), so a report can be wrong about the code. It runs when `select` or `extend-select` names its code or name, and with `lint.heuristic = true` (`--heuristic`) also by default and for its prefixes and `ALL`. Of 20 sampled reports (round 3, 2026-11-21), 70% were right about the code. See [Rule Precision](../precision.md).

## What it does
Checks mutations of objects returned by a shared producer:

- functions decorated with `@functools.lru_cache` / `@functools.cache` (every caller receives
  the same object), also through an import alias (`lru_cache as _lru_cache`); a `cache`
  decorator the module defines itself is not one;
- producers declared in `[[tool.heki.readonly-returns]]`;
- functions that return a producer's value, or a part of it, on some path: a wrapper is a
  producer itself, without configuration, through any number of wrappers, property getters,
  and recursion.

Mutations through attributes, subscripts, container methods, in-place operators, and helpers
that mutate their argument (also run on a worker thread: `asyncio.to_thread(clear, shared)`) are
followed, also on the call result itself
(`schema_of(raw).items.append(x)`); a generator function mutates its argument only when its
generator is iterated. Copies end the protection: `copy.deepcopy(...)`,
`model.model_copy(deep=True)` (without `update=`, whose values Pydantic assigns to the copy by
reference), and the deep copy sanitizers of the ecosystem knowledge base clear it, shallow copies
(`copy.copy`, `.copy()`, `dataclasses.replace(...)`, `dict(...)`, `list(...)`, `tuple(...)`,
`set(...)`, `frozenset(...)`, displays that only unpack the value (`{**shared}`, `[*rows]`), a
sanitizer declared `copy-sanitizer = "shallow"`, and slices of builtin lists, other builtin
sequences, and values whose class heki cannot infer, `rows()[:]`) free the top level only: the
values below stay shared, so a helper rebinding an attribute of the copy (`b.name = "new"`)
changes nothing shared, and one changing the object an attribute holds (`b.tags.append(x)`, also
on its own shallow copy of the argument) does. A slice of an object of another known class may
be a view of it (`numpy`) and stays shared. A `copy()` method of a project class copies as
deeply as its body does: its result is shared only when the method returns a shared value. A
wrapper that returns a copy on one path and the shared value on another still returns a shared
value.

Filling a memo of the shared object, directly or in a method or helper it is handed to, is no
mutation: an in-place change of an attribute named as a cache or memo (`self._style_cache[k] =
v`, also through the methods of a cache object held there), a store under
`if k not in self._decoders:` or through `setdefault`, and a lazy
initialization (`if self._runtime is None: self._runtime = load()`) leave what the object
computes as it was.

## What a report states

A report states that the function changes in place an object that a shared producer returned: a
function decorated with `@functools.lru_cache` / `@functools.cache`, a producer declared in
`readonly-returns`, or a function returning a producer's value.

Its premises:

- **Producer**: the decorator, known by what its name is bound to, or the declaration. Established.
- **Returned through wrappers**: a function returning a producer's value on some path is a producer.
  Open: one path is enough.
- **Same object**: the changed object is the returned one, or an object below it, not a copy. Open:
  a value that is the shared one on one path counts.
- **Changed in place**: a store, a mutator, an in-place operator, or a helper changing its argument.
  The memo fills listed above are left out; a memo fill heki does not recognize does change the
  object.

## Why is this bad?
A cached return value is shared by every caller. Mutating it corrupts the cache for everyone
else, usually long after the mutation happened.

## Example
```python
from functools import lru_cache


@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def schema(name: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    return {"fields": [name]}


def schema_of(name: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    return schema(name)


def extend(name: str) -> None:
    s = schema_of(name)
    s["fields"].append("extra")  # MUT202: mutates the cached object
```

Use instead:
```python
import copy


def extend(name: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    s = copy.deepcopy(schema_of(name))
    s["fields"].append("extra")
    return s
```

## Known limitations
- A shared value stored in an attribute (`self.kept = schema(...)`) and changed in another
  method is not followed.
- A generator's values and a coroutine's result (`await`) are not followed.
- A method call on a shared value whose class heki cannot resolve (a producer returning a type
  variable) is not followed; a wrapper with a concrete return annotation resolves it.
- A dict that also holds values of its own (`{**shared, "extra": []}`,
  `dict(shared, extra=[])`) or unpacks another mapping (`{**shared, **overrides}`) is not
  followed.
- A project method returning a part of a shared receiver (`return self._items[key]`) is not
  followed, nor is a `copy()` method of a project class that shares the receiver's values
  (`return Post(self.tags)`).

## Fix safety
No automatic fix.

## Options
- `[[tool.heki.readonly-returns]]`: `name`, `producers` (function names or globs), `deep`
  (protect nested values too).
